ranking.rationale: Earlier slot keeps the arrival stream regular and adds no airborne time or taxi load; dest_disruption=4 is low relative to nominal_aar=45 (assumed).
Small earlier shift disturbs the stream least and avoids added taxi and holding at the destination.
Small later shift keeps the stream regular with no airborne holding; wake_category=L (assumed) is a light category needing less margin.
Holding at origin keeps the aircraft off destination-side taxiways and avoids airborne holds, though the 45-min delay is long.
Larger later shift is still a slot change with no airborne holding, but disturbs the schedule more than smaller shifts.
Adds 2 min of extra taxi, slightly adding to taxiway load under taxi_congestion=1.29.
Adds 5 min of extra taxi, more taxiway load than C2 under taxi_congestion=1.29.
Airborne hold adds aircraft into the final approach stream, disturbing sector throughput; tolerable only because dest_disruption=4 is low.
Longer airborne hold puts more traffic into the stream and on final; least preferred acceptable option for my domain.
Diversion disturbs the arrival stream most; no destination disruption in the data justifies it.
Diversion disturbs the arrival stream most and is the longest delay; no destination disruption in the data justifies it.

vetoes.reason: Diverting is the most disruptive option to sector throughput and destination disruption is low.
Diverting is the most disruptive option to sector throughput and destination disruption is low.

ranking.rationale: Earlier arrival adds no airborne time and gives the lowest est_knock_on_min, protecting connections; fuel_reserve_min is only estimated so no fuel draw is preferred.
Earlier arrival with no holding fuel draw and a lower knock-on than the baseline, though the duty and weather exposure is still present.
Holding on the ground at origin draws no airborne fuel and keeps the flight out of the weather at DEN, though it adds 45 minutes to duty.
Only 2 extra taxi minutes with no airborne time; small knock-on impact.
5 extra taxi minutes with no airborne fuel draw; acceptable but less favourable than C2.
Adds 15 minutes of delay and draws some time on the day, but avoids holding in weather at DEN.
Airborne holding near DEN in weather draws on the estimated fuel reserve and adds turbulence exposure.
Largest slot delay that avoids airborne holding, but the knock-on to connections is significant.
Avoids the weather but adds a second approach, extra fuel burn on an estimated reserve, and loses all connections; nearest alternate.
Forty minutes of airborne holding in weather draws heavily on an estimated fuel reserve and is the most exposed option.
Longest diversion with the highest est_delay and loses all connections, adding a second approach on an estimated fuel reserve.

vetoes.reason: Forty minutes of airborne holding near DEN in weather draws on the estimated fuel reserve and is the most exposed place to be.
Far alternate with the largest delay and loss of all connections; a second approach on an estimated fuel reserve is not justified.

ranking.rationale: Lowest est_knock_on_min on the menu, and an earlier slot keeps the turnaround off the congested ramp.
Second-lowest est_knock_on_min and an earlier arrival, limiting ramp load at the current taxi_congestion.
Gate swap with the lowest added taxi and second-lowest knock-on among gate options; gate model is synthetic, so C2 availability needs confirming.
Gate swap is workable but adds more extra taxi than C2 and a higher knock-on; synthetic gate data.
Delay adds ground-crew knock-on and lands into the current ramp peak.
Holding aircraft in the air adds knock-on and ramp exposure at peak.
Longer delay pushes turnaround toward the next shift with high knock-on.
Long hold with high knock-on; acceptable only as a fallback to landing at DEN.
Hold at the origin of downstream_legs[1] adds knock-on; tolerable only as a fallback to landing at DEN.
Diversion strands the tail and the gate plan and breaks the downstream legs out of DEN.
Diversion strands the tail and downstream legs; highest knock-on on the menu.

vetoes.reason: Diversion strands the tail, the gate plan and the downstream legs departing DEN.
Diversion strands the tail and downstream legs and carries the highest est_knock_on_min.

ranking.rationale: Earlier slot moves the arrival away from the destination peak and keeps the stream regular; wake spacing benefits from the shift.
Smaller earlier shift keeps the stream regular and avoids taxiway load at the peak.
Later slot shift is a small stream disturbance and keeps aircraft off the taxiways, though it adds to the destination hour.
Larger later shift disturbs the stream more than the 15-minute option and adds to the destination hour.
Ground hold at origin keeps the aircraft off DEN taxiways and airborne, so it is good for taxi flow, but it is a long hold.
Short extra taxi adds some taxiway time at the destination but no airborne disturbance.
Longer extra taxi than C2 adds more taxiway occupancy at a congested field.
Airborne hold feeds the disrupted arrival peak and disturbs the sector stream.
Longest airborne hold puts the aircraft into the destination peak and disturbs the stream most among holds.
Diversion disturbs the arrival stream most; destination disruption is low, so no diversion is needed to protect final spacing. Veto stands.
Largest delay and stream disturbance with no runway-side benefit over local options.

vetoes.reason: Round-2 concession not given: PILOT accepts this diversion, but I keep the round-1 veto because destination disruption is low and a diversion disturbs the arrival stream most.
Diversion gives the largest stream disturbance with no runway benefit over the slot and hold options.

ranking.rationale: Earliest-arrival-protecting option that adds no airborne time; keeps fuel_reserve_min=89.1 (estimated) undrawn.
Shorter slot shift, no airborne hold, keeps fuel and duty margin largely intact.
Only 2 extra taxi minutes; no airborne time added, though WEATHER_DELAY=367 is present so ground time is preferred.
Holds on ground at origin, away from weather exposure; draws no airborne fuel but is a 45-minute delay.
Five extra taxi minutes, no airborne fuel draw; acceptable but slightly less than C2.
Later arrival erodes connection margin; no fuel draw but adds duty time.
Later arrival than SLOT+15 with no fuel draw; connection margins at risk and duty time grows.
Airborne hold near destination in weather draws on fuel_reserve_min=89.1 (estimated) and adds turbulence exposure.
Withdrawn veto, accepted only as a last resort: 40 min airborne in weather draws on fuel_reserve_min=89.1 (estimated) and is the most exposed option.
Nearest alternate, but a second approach and loss of all listed connections; fuel draw on alternates[0].distance_nm=63.2.
Farther alternate adds second approach and loses all connections; ATC and GROUND both oppose it.

vetoes.reason: Longer diversion than COS, a second approach and loss of all connections; both other agents also oppose it.

ranking.rationale: Earliest slot gives the lowest est_knock_on_min on the menu and keeps the tail on the downstream LAS/DEN rotation.
Early slot with low est_knock_on_min and no added ramp taxi; keeps the gate plan intact.
Gate swap to C2 uses a free gate with only 2 min extra taxi (synthetic gate model, turnaround_source=assumed).
Free gate D6 is workable but adds 5 min taxi on a congested ramp.
Moderate delay with higher est_knock_on_min than the early slots; acceptable as a fallback.
Airborne hold adds delay and knock-on; tolerable if slot options are unavailable.
Larger slot delay with high est_knock_on_min; accepted only as a concession.
Longest hold with high est_knock_on_min; accepted only as a concession to keep the hub landing.
45 min ground hold at LAS is outside DEN gate control and carries high est_knock_on_min on the DEN-LAS-DEN rotation.
Kept vetoed: diversion strands the tail and downstream legs; the only other agent acceptance is PILOT's, and no other agent's acceptable id is outside my list, so no widening is possible here.
Vetoed: largest est_knock_on_min and est_delay_min on the menu, with the tail stranded away from the hub.

vetoes.reason: Diversion strands the tail and downstream legs; kept veto because no other agent accepts an id outside my acceptable list that I had not vetoed.
Largest knock-on on the menu and strands the tail away from the hub.
